newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung flies to Beijing for handover talks.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung flies to Beijing for handover talks.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa flew to Beijing on Wednesday for talks on the territory's July 1 takeover by China, a spokesman said.

Tung was due to meet Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, the architect of China's policies on Hong Kong, and the head of Beijing's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, Lu Ping, as well as other senior Chinese officials, the spokesman said.

Britain is handing Hong Kong back to China at midnight on June 30 after 156 years of colonial rule. It will become a quasi autonomous capitalist region of communist-ruled China, with Beijing-appointed Tung as its first post-colonial leader.
Tung is widely expected to discuss with Qian the contentious issue of plans to curb civil liberties, the subject of a major public consultation exercise in Hong Kong over the past month.
Hong Kong is deeply split over Tung's plan to curb the right to protest and ban foreign funding of local political groups.
"We don't know his exact agenda in Beijing," the Tung aide said. "He is going to cover transition matters involving China, Hong Kong and Britain, and it could cover anything."
Tung will return to Hong Kong later in the day.
